_doc: contours of record transcribed from the printed tables 2026-09-18 (pdftotext,
two rows of Table 2 split by the layout re-typed by hand; Table 3 rows whose
columns the layout broke are absent -- 17 of its rows kept, the last one
(11.51781, 1.37506) included). Columns x [in], y [in], wall angle [deg]. Posing
p. 1586: p_c 500 psia, T_c 6000 R, R 56 ft-lbf/(lbm-R), gamma 1.23, mdot 148.08
lbm/s, p_a 14.7 psia, L(T->D) 12 in, base Eq. (12) Veen, C_f 0.002.
_knot_class_note: the class within which a walk 'stays' on a table's contour: the S31 table-start landing on Table 2 put every knot but the first within 0.05-0.15 in (the first at +0.34 in = the planar inlet), so 0.15 in is the measured stay class; cls EMPIRICAL
_throat_mean_radius_note: p. 1586: "a mean radius of curvature at the throat of 0.705 in." -- the input of their modified Moore-Hall transonic start line; the MEAN of the two walls in the Moore-Hall sense (harmonic: R_c of Dutton = R_mean / separation whatever the split between the walls, the split setting only the asymmetry K); cls SPEC
_downstream_radius_note: p. 1586: "a downstream radius of curvature of 0.5 in." -- the prescribed plug arc from the start-line point A to the point T where the optimised contour begins (p. 1585: the curvature is specified so that no corner arises at T, and T is always downstream of A); cls SPEC
_table_precision_note: the printed digits of Tables 2-3 (x, y to 1e-5 in, angles to 1e-5 deg); cls SPEC
_lip_precision_note: the cowl lip radius is printed as 7.55 in (two decimals): half a unit in the last place; cls SPEC
_length_TD_precision_note: p. 1586 prints the length T -> D as 12.0 in (one decimal): half a unit in the last place; cls SPEC
_grid_class_note: Table 1 p. 1586: their own 20-run grid on the (injection angle, lip radius) plane spans 32,699..32,877 lbf around the optimum, 0.54 percent -- the flatness of THEIR functional at THEIR own resolution, quoted beside our march's band in stage grad; cls SPEC (their printed table)
_table3_recovered_rows_note: Table 3 p. 1587: the two rows whose columns the PDF layout broke and the 2026-09-18 transcription left out (x, y, wall angle; x from the lip, inches/deg), recovered from the text layer of the same PDF on 2026-09-22 (S33): at x 4.04195 the angle sits on the line above its x/y pair, at x 9.28531 the x sits on the line below its y/angle pair. Kept OUT of table3_rao_lip8.33_inj-58.5 so that every S31 reading of record (the knots read by chords) stays bit-identical; table3_complete() in a1_humphreys_twin.py joins them. cls SPEC (their printed table)
_table3_typo_note: Table 3 p. 1587 prints -12.27169 deg at x 5.33714 inside a column that rises monotonically from -60.69 at the foot through -25.23198 (x 4.04195) to -20.07902 (x 6.55991): a one-digit misprint for -22.27169, which restores the monotone column and sits against our ideal member where its neighbours do (stage rao R-5). Found by the S32 session (2026-09-22) and confirmed by S33; the transcription above is faithful to the print. Any reader that uses Table 3's angle column (the Hermite mode of read_table) must take the corrected value. cls EMPIRICAL (an inference from their own column, not a printed number)
